A module opens a modal by calling `showModal(name, props, onClose?)` with the name it registered in `routes.json`. That call returns a `close` function, which the module calls to close the modal. The framework also passes the same function into the modal as its `close` prop.

**Registration.** The app declares the modal in the `modals` section of `routes.json`, with a `name` ending in `-modal` and a `component`. The framework's route loader turns each entry into a `registerModal` call that stores it by name (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-routes/src/loaders/components.ts`, lines 80–103). The store lives in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-extensions/src/modals.ts` (lines 17–27). Registering a modal as an extension still works but is deprecated and logs a warning (`modals.ts` lines 29–48).

**Opening.** `showModal` in `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-styleguide/src/modals/index.tsx` (lines 293–319) does the following:
- It builds a `close` closure that finds the stack entry whose `onClose` matches and closes it.
- If no registration exists for the name, it reports an error and does not throw.
- Otherwise it pushes a `NEW` instance onto the modal stack and passes `{ close, ...props }` to the modal as props.
- It returns `close`.

**Closing.** `closeInstance` (lines 236–250) marks the instance `TO_BE_DELETED` and republishes the stack. The render pass in `handleModalStateUpdate` (lines 123–224) then calls `onClose`, unmounts the parcel, removes the DOM frame and drops the entry from the stack. `closeHighestInstance` and `handleEscKey` (lines 252–265) close the top modal on Escape.

**Documentation.** The modal system guide is at `openmrs-contrib-o3-docs/content/en-US/docs/modal-system.mdx`. Its registration section is at lines 45–84, and the `onClose` callback section is at lines 92–104. The API reference for `showModal` is generated at `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-framework/docs/functions/showModal.md`.

**Example caller.** `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-common-lib/src/launchStartVisitPrompt.tsx` (lines 3–8) opens `start-visit-dialog` and passes its own `closeModal: () => dispose()`, so the modal can close itself through the returned function.

I did not read the "`close` prop" section at the end of the docs page (after line 129), so I have not verified its wording.
